state.context: The current Qualification is an Invoice-owned declaration without a producer. Invoice owns Customer invoices and real collected/refunded amounts, Rent owns booking completion, and Member owns term cancellation status. CanRefer already checks exclusive_program/account but lacks captured-time and first-customer evidence. Public referral codes carry no authentication. Draft-only workflows may be changed; no running adapters or new infrastructure are in scope.
state.candidate: Keep one authoritative first-customer decision over Invoice customer commercial history. Refer captures a code only for a verified Customer account and retains the last capture within its window. Rent and Member freeze that Capture into their sale and emit source milestones. Invoice verifies frozen source/amount/customer against its payment ledger and publishes Qualification after payment and milestone evidence agree. Customer history must be explicitly complete; absent legacy baseline is unknown and cannot earn a first-customer reward. A monotone source record preserves reversal-before-qualification and rejects conflicting replay.

ownership.instructions: Select the owner strategy that best preserves verified new-customer eligibility, replay safety, implementation economy and customer privacy.

criteria.invoice: Invoice combines its authoritative payment history with source-owned milestones and verified Refer capture. Requires narrow source integration and a reviewed historical baseline; gives one cross-product eligibility decision.
criteria.source: Rent and Member each decide new-customer qualification from their own payment/completion records and capture. Reduces centralized work, but requires synchronizing history across products to avoid inconsistent first-customer decisions.
criteria.consumer: Refer accepts a source first_customer boolean and captured time without checking authoritative history. Keeps consumers compact and shifts correctness entirely to an explicitly implemented trusted producer.
